newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Tietmeyer - stability pact clearly political.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Tietmeyer - stability pact clearly political.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer on Thursday said that the stability pact agreed by European Union finance ministers in Dublin earlier this month was a political matter on which central bankers had no direct influence.
"(That) is a clear political decision," Tietmeyer told a news conference, adding that benkers could only advise on such a pact.

He added that certain "key elements" had been set in Dublin such as the aim of balanced budgets and noted that it was important that the three percent deficit-to-GDP (Gross Domestic Product) criteria had been set as a maximum there.
"Overall I think in Dublin the central significance of clear budgetary discipline was recognised, he said.
Tietmeter said he welcomed the fact that the European union Council made the need for long-term stability clear.
